content.body: * In July, 1939, petrol was rationed to 200 miles per month. * Brand names disappeared, only 'Pool' petrol was available at four shillings and two pence a gallon. * In 1940, the manufacture of new cars was stopped. * In 1942, petrol for private use was disallowed. * The average wage in 1939 for men was £3 and nine shillings. * The average wage in 1939 for women was £1 and twelve shillings. * For newly-enlisted servicemen, the pay was two shillings a day. * A bottle of whisky cost 13 shillings and sixpence. * The price of gold was £8 an ounce. * To conserve wood, the Government requested all women to wear flat-heeled shoes and light clothes in order to save dye for forces uniforms. Many non-essential factories were closed.
